clue.text: Notedly brisk

parts.note: brisk in the world of musical notes: the Italian tempo marking a score uses for a lively pace

explanation.surface: Someone is quick and businesslike, as everyone remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notedly' looks like 'noticeably', but it means 'in terms of musical notes', so the clue asks for a tempo direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning fast and lively, printed on scores to set a brisk pace.

clue.text: A number rule out showing charm

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a number

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the four letters of rule are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A regulation is dropped because it seemed attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges RULE into LURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: attraction or fascinating appeal, the power to draw people in.

clue.text: Yet all has been changed in recent times

indicators.note: the letters of the two words before have been altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Despite everything, life has been different over the last while.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: of late, during the period just past.

clue.text: Environmentally friendly residence that's of growing importance

parts.note: green means kind to the environment
a house is a residence

explanation.surface: An eco-friendly home is becoming more and more significant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of growing importance' seems to mean increasingly significant; it is a glass building whose importance lies in growing plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazed building where plants are raised, so its whole purpose is cultivation of seedlings and crops.

clue.text: Form of louse, one with wings

indicators.note: a form of a word is that word reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind of louse that can fly.
explanation.walkthrough: A louse is wingless, so the surface is a little absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackbird or similar thrush, a bird and so a creature that has wings.

clue.text: No corner stones?

parts.note: stones with no corners: small rounded ones worn smooth by water

explanation.surface: Is a building missing its cornerstones?
explanation.walkthrough: 'corner stones' suggests foundation blocks in a building; read literally, it means stones that have no corners.
explanation.definitionFit: Small stones smoothed and rounded by water on beaches and riverbeds, so they have no angular edges.

clue.text: Two synonyms for 'iron' used in journalists' association

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them; an iron is also a golf club
to iron clothes is to press them; an iron is also a golf club

explanation.surface: A puzzle-like instruction: find two words for iron, used by a reporters' body.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, an iron is a type of club.
explanation.definitionFit: A social and professional club for reporters and newspaper people, the press being journalists collectively.

clue.text: Cricketers attempt to get a rise

indicators.note: in a down answer a word that rises is read from bottom to top, so it runs backwards

parts.note: a stab is an attempt, as in have a stab at it

explanation.surface: Players try to provoke a reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting players are called bats.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket jargon, batsmen are often called bats, as in a team's top-order bats.

clue.text: Bird we see settle on perch?

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sitting on another is placed above it

parts.note: to land is to settle after flying
a rail is somewhere to perch

explanation.surface: A bird we watch coming down to roost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' looks like a verb; it is a noun, the rail.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the corncrake, a bird of the rail family that lives in grassland.

clue.text: Crooked city runs investigation

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A corrupt town is under inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: close examination or careful inspection of something.

clue.text: Turner puts together bilingual articles

parts.note: the definite article in two languages: la in French and the in English
the definite article in two languages: la in French and the in English

explanation.surface: The painter Turner assembles articles in two languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter, but it is a machine that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that spins wood or metal against a cutting tool, so it is something that turns.

clue.text: Somehow resent accepting small bribe

indicators.note: the scrambled word takes in another piece, holding it inside
somehow signals the letters are put together in some other way

parts.note: taken as written
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Someone feels resentful about taking a little backhander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small bribe' reads as one phrase, but 'small' belongs to the wordplay. 'Somehow' gives STENER, which 'accepting' opens after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: an inducement or payment offered to win someone over.

clue.text: Brutal advice to those who yield too easily

definitions.text: advice to those who yield too easily
definitions.meaning: read in two parts, it tells pushovers to give in to a smaller extent

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and it is advice: relent less often.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unremitting and pitiless, never easing off, which is what brutal suggests.

clue.text: Expression of annoyance at which doctor starts

indicators.note: the doctor piece starts the answer, coming before the other word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient's cry of irritation makes the physician jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' looks like jumps in surprise; it means the doctor comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild exclamation of irritation, like dash it or blast.

clue.text: Family man, perhaps, holds post up for the house

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other within it

parts.note: a parent is an example of a family man, hence perhaps

indicators.note: in a down answer a word written up runs backwards

parts.note: mail is post

explanation.surface: A father, maybe, keeps the post for the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family man' is a parent only by example, hence 'perhaps'; 'up' gives LIAM, which 'holds' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislative assembly; in Britain the Commons and the Lords are each called the House.

clue.text: Discussion with a specialist involved coolant units

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A meeting with an expert concerned refrigeration equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting to seek expert advice, such as a medical appointment with a hospital doctor.

clue.text: Graphic new form of catechism

indicators.note: a new form of a word gives its letters a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An illustration presents a modern version of a religious instruction text.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the noun sense: a diagram showing the layout of a system in simplified form.

clue.text: Drink after start of race the Queen presents

indicators.note: the drink comes after the other pieces

parts.note: they're off is the call at the start of a horse race
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: The monarch offers a drink once the race has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of race' looks like it wants the letter R, but it is OFF, as in they're off.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal synonym: offers up or presents something, often as a sacrifice or a gift.

clue.text: Road led fancifully round city of gold

indicators.note: fancifully suggests letters set out in an imaginative new order

parts.note: taken as written
a round shape looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: The way ran in a whimsical loop around a gilded city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancifully' rearranges ROADLED into ELDORAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary South American place of gold sought by Spanish explorers.

clue.text: Provides what is necessary and tops up the account

definitions.meaning: an idiom for being exactly what is needed
literally adds to an invoice, packing it up to the full amount

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom literally, as stuffing a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: is suitable or satisfies the requirements, exactly meeting the need.

clue.text: Young Christopher has to catch up young Tom

parts.note: Kit is a diminutive, pet form of the name Christopher

indicators.note: in a down answer a word written up runs backwards

parts.note: to net is to catch

explanation.surface: Little Christopher has to catch up with young Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NET into TEN. 'Tom' looks like a boy's name; a tom is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cat; a tom is a male cat, so a young tom is a baby cat.

clue.text: Honours damsel in distress

indicators.note: a word in distress is in a bad way, so its letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A knight is decorated for rescuing a damsel in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damsel in distress' reads as a fixed phrase, but 'in distress' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal decorations awarded as distinctions, which are honours.

clue.text: Cupid's painful back

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round, written in the other direction

parts.note: sore means painful

explanation.surface: Cupid has a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painful back' reads as a sore spine; 'back' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love, equivalent to the Roman Cupid.

clue.text: Critical mood

definitions.meaning: in grammar, the verb form used for commands

explanation.definitionFit: Synonym for vital, and also the grammatical term for the command form of a verb.

clue.text: Turn out not as agreed

parts.note: to throw a tenant out of a property, against what the tenancy agreed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out' looks like 'prove to be', as in a plan that turned out badly; it means expel.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel a tenant from a property by legal process, breaking the occupancy.

clue.text: In poor health, creature that can't fly

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An animal unable to fly because it is unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flightless South American bird, similar to an ostrich.

clue.text: You may wind up eating it

definitions.text: You may wind up eating it

parts.words: You may wind up eating it
parts.note: a food twirled round a fork before it is eaten

explanation.walkthrough: 'wind up' looks like 'end up'; it means twist round a fork.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin strings of pasta, eaten by twirling them round a fork.

clue.text: One may add to the score without being a hit at cricket

definitions.text: One may add to the score without being a hit at cricket

parts.words: One may add to the score without being a hit at cricket
parts.note: a run in cricket not scored off the bat, such as a wide or a bye

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs given away by the fielding side (wides, no-balls, byes) count for the batting team though no one hit the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket term for a run credited to the batting team that the batter did not hit.

clue.text: Boring press officers one's taken into account

parts.note: PROs are public relations officers, who handle the press

indicators.note: one piece is taken into another and sits inside it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Dull publicity people have a single item on their bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken into' puts I inside AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dull and commonplace, lacking imagination or excitement.

clue.text: Aunt set about making complaint

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A relative begins grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like a grumble; here it means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint in the medical sense: an illness, here lockjaw, a bacterial infection.
